description: The nine canonical system.* modules -> exact MCP primitive, name/URI. Pins aiperceivable/apcore-mcp#15's classification table (system.health.*/system.usage.*/system.manifest.* are resources or resource templates; system.control.* stays a tool) and operationalizes the issue's 'byte-identical tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list across TypeScript, Python and Rust' acceptance criterion: given a registry produced by the SAME real registerSysModules()/register_sys_modules() call (sys_modules.enabled=true, sys_modules.events.enabled=true), each adapter's own tool/resource projection MUST produce exactly the entries below -- not merely an equivalent shape. A single-language fix (e.g. only one adapter emitting the RFC 6570 '{?period}' query-expansion on a template) is exactly the drift this fixture exists to catch.
spec: PROTOCOL_SPEC.md#6.6.2 (classification by module_id prefix only), aiperceivable/apcore-mcp#15 (URI convention table), aiperceivable/apcore-mcp#16 Phase A (surfaces grouping)

setup.description: Build the registry that produces all nine module ids: sys_modules.enabled=true AND sys_modules.events.enabled=true. Without the events flag only the six read-only modules register and 'system.control.*' matches nothing -- see aiperceivable/apcore-mcp#15's registration-ladder table (0 / 6 / 9 modules).

resource_templates.note: The only one of the nine modules whose declared template carries the RFC 6570 form-style query expansion '{?period}' -- system.usage.summary's optional ?period= is accepted at read time but is NOT part of its (non-template) resource's declared uri, since a concrete Resource.uri cannot carry template syntax.

extension.description: With every system.* module registered (this fixture's setup), all four surfaces are present -- so the extension MUST be advertised with surfaces == surface_order verbatim.
